source: NazoNazo authors, JAIST (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles Reveal Fundamental Limits of Machine Insight and Self-Evaluation
finding: Insight-style riddle benchmark. Most of 38 LLMs fall far below humans, zero-shot, no retrieval. Reasoning models do better than non-reasoning ones.
numbers: 201 riddles; 120-item human subset, human n=126, mean 52.9% (95% CI 46.6-59.2). Non-reasoning models mean 7.6%, reasoning models 17.6% on subset. Full 201 items: 9.42% vs 19.25%, OR 2.29 (95% CI 1.99-2.64). GPT-5 alone fell inside the human CI. Parameter count did not predict accuracy; release date did.
limits: Single language (Japanese); overlap with human CI is not equivalence; no model-by-model tests.
agent_relevance: Plain pass rate on insight-type items is low; the S0 gate should expect low base rates and not trust one sample.

source: NazoNazo authors, JAIST (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles Reveal Fundamental Limits of Machine Insight and Self-Evaluation
finding: Verification failure: the model writes the correct answer in its thought log, then does not endorse it and answers wrong. This is a monitoring failure, not a generation failure.
numbers: Share of each model's wrong answers that contained a gold answer in the log: Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview 5.23% (9 cases), DeepSeek-R1-0528 30.57% (48), Claude Opus 4 25.00% (35), Grok 4 39.34% (48). Grok 4: 72 correct, 48 VF, 194 answered.
quote: verification failures accounted for between 5% and 39% of a model's incorrect answers
limits: Counted by literal string match of gold answer in the log, so a mention may be incidental; only 4 models had usable logs; accuracy there differs from main scoring.
agent_relevance: Directly supports S4 harvesting: code should extract every candidate raised in the trace and test it, not rely on the model to endorse its own best candidate.

source: NazoNazo authors, JAIST (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles Reveal Fundamental Limits of Machine Insight and Self-Evaluation
finding: Models also show a false-insight pattern: they lock onto a wrong reinterpretation with apparent confidence and stop. Authors call it analogous to human false aha, descriptively only.
numbers: Qualitative thought-log cases; no rate reported for false insight.
limits: Analogy only, no mechanism claim; no counts.
agent_relevance: Confidence at the moment of commitment is not a signal of correctness: supports G10 and the ban on self-reported warmth or certainty.

source: NazoNazo authors, JAIST (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles Reveal Fundamental Limits of Machine Insight and Self-Evaluation
finding: Few-shot demonstrations that include reasoning improved accuracy in all four tested models, significant in two. Language of the thought log (Japanese vs English) did not reliably help.
numbers: Supplementary study, four models. Grok 4 did worse when thinking in Japanese (29.5% vs 48.8%, p=0.0071); Claude Opus 4 36.7% vs 28.7% (p=0.356).
limits: Improvement not uniform and not shown across several demonstration sets; details in SI Appendix 5.
agent_relevance: Worked reasoning examples may raise search or checking quality; test inside S3 only if it pays at equal tokens (G7).

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models
finding: Mid-trace reasoning shifts (Wait, Aha) are rare, do not grow with training, and mostly hurt accuracy. Formal Aha moments are rarer still.
numbers: Over 1M traces; about 6.31% of traces shift (pooled); formal Aha 1.79%. Qwen2.5-1.5B pooled: 2.57% correct with a shift vs 16.44% without (N=723,200). MATH-500 with vs without shift: Qwen2.5-7B 28.2 vs 66.1; GPT-4o 33.8 vs 65.8; DeepSeek-R1 20.4 vs 54.3; Llama3.1-8B 28.2 vs 45.7. Cryptic crosswords exception: 20.1 vs 9.6.
limits: Shift detection by lexical cues and a judge (kappa 0.79 on MATH-500); page text has internal inconsistencies; only 3 checkable domains; correlational because shifted traces are harder items.
agent_relevance: The model's own felt aha in the trace is a poor signal; do not trigger or trust it. Matches G1 and G10.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models (triggered shifts)
finding: Externally triggered reconsideration at moments of high token entropy raises accuracy, while intrinsic shifts do not. A code-chosen trigger beats a model-chosen one.
numbers: Qwen2.5-1.5B, MATH-500: 32.21% to 40.62% (+8.41 pp); 50,574 wrong-to-right vs 23,500 right-to-wrong flips. Crosswords +0.45 pp (9.70 to 10.15). RHour +0.01 pp. Intrinsic shifts in top-20% entropy traces -7.40 pp vs -22.88 pp at low entropy on Math.
limits: Gain concentrated in math with a small model; appendix tables for high-entropy subsets not read; prompt-level cue, no causal mechanism.
agent_relevance: Best direct support for an S6 impasse detector run by code from entropy and outcomes, not from the model's self-report.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Understanding Aha Moments: from External Observations to Internal Mechanisms
finding: Distilled R1-style models use more hesitation words (Wait, Hmm) as problems get harder; instruct models do not. Difficulty is encoded in early layers of aha models.
numbers: Knights and Knaves and Count Down, difficulty n=3 to 10; 100 questions per level for token analysis, 200 per level for collapse tests. RASM score crosses zero for aha models, stays negative for no-aha. 4 model pairs, 1.5B to 14B. Silhouette scores near zero (peak 0.0067 to 0.0103).
limits: No accuracy reported; models differ in base and training; token lists chosen by hand; correlation only.
agent_relevance: Hesitation language tracks task difficulty, so it could feed a cheap difficulty signal into S0 budget choice, but it is not proof of progress.

source: Tsui (2025) Self-Correction Bench: Revealing and Addressing the Self-Correction Blind Spot in LLMs
finding: Models fix an injected error in a user's text but not the same error in their own output. Appending Wait cuts the blind spot.
numbers: 14 open models; average blind spot 64.5%. Wait reduced it by 89.3% and raised mean accuracy by 156.0%. Items: SCLI5 286, GSM8K-SC 1,313, PRM800K-SC 448.
limits: Injected errors may differ from natural ones; temperature 0; math and simple tasks; Gemini auto-judge with 100 samples checked per set; no closed models.
agent_relevance: Monitoring is weak on own output. Show the located failing output as if from outside (G2, S5), and let code decide when to cue a recheck.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty
finding: Verbalised uncertainty tokens (wait, perhaps) restore information gain after a wrong path. Masking them hurts.
numbers: Masking epistemic tokens at test time: about -25% (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B), -19% (14B). From 1.5B to 14B: Wait +75%, Perhaps +235% on AIME24. Qwen3-14B-Base AIME24 pass@1: base 16.7, LIMO 60.0, self-distillation 3.3.
limits: Theory limited to closed-world settings; tokens are crude proxies for latent epistemic state; authors warn of overtrust in verbose traces.
agent_relevance: Competing view: some uncertainty talk helps. Use as a reason to test, not to add scheduled doubt (G1).

source: Stumpers study authors (2023) LLMs versus humans on stumpers, EMNLP Findings
finding: Stumpers (single-step riddles with a misleading first representation): newer chat models beat humans at solving but are worse than humans at telling right from wrong.
numbers: Humans (n=81) solved 38.15%, replicating 35% from Bar-Hillel 2021. GPT-3.5/GPT-4 mean 57.8% (original set), 43.4% (enhanced); Davinci-2/3 29.6% and 22.5%. Verification from two options: humans 100% when they could solve, 63.8% when they could not; most models below chance (mean 41%). Davinci-3 verified at 70% (ground truth) and 85% (own answer vs truth).
limits: Four models, 2023 versions; prompt helped GPT-3 and hurt chat models (interaction F(1,4)=30.82, p=0.005); small number of stumpers.
agent_relevance: Humans recognise a right answer they could not produce; chat models do not. Never let the generator select among candidates (G5, G8); verification must be by code or a blind check.

source: Only Connect Wall authors (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings
finding: Red herrings (plausible wrong groupings) cause fixation in LLMs, as in the human Einstellung effect. Removing herrings raises scores.
numbers: GPT-4 0-shot grouping first-metric 75.8 in one table row; connection F1 41-45% with 10-shot GPT-4 vs human about 80%. Scores rose significantly in OCW-Randomized and OCW-WordNet where herrings were diluted or removed. Error sources: 4.4% misformatted, 6.6% hallucinated clues.
limits: Word-grouping task, not classic insight problems; some table columns not cleanly parsed from the PDF.
agent_relevance: Fixation is a model trait too; supports S3 fresh-context attempts and history tracking (links to the Einstellung subfield).

source: Hedne, Norman and Metcalfe (2016) Intuitive feelings of warmth and confidence in insight and noninsight problem solving of magic tricks
finding: Human reference: insight solutions get higher confidence yet metacognitive accuracy is at chance for insight and above chance for noninsight. Warmth did not separate the two (no replication of Metcalfe and Wiebe 1987).
numbers: N=51, 32 magic tricks, 971 trials (281 insight). Accuracy .57 vs .37 (d=0.51). Confidence 78.32 vs 68.95 (d=0.50). Az: insight 0.56 (not above chance), noninsight 0.64 (p<.001); between-type p=.297. Warmth: differential 2.92 vs 0.30, p=.429.
limits: About 70% of trials dropped for warmth (3-4 ratings per trial vs up to 40 in 1987); insight self-reported; one stimulus set.
agent_relevance: Human anchor for the guardrail: felt confidence is higher but no more accurate on insight items. Models show the same shape (high confidence, wrong).

source: Webb, Little and Cropper (2016) Insight Is Not in the Problem
finding: Whether a solution is insight depends on the solver, not the problem. Aha tracks accuracy within each task type.
numbers: Exp 1: 193 recruited (9 removed); Exp 1a: 82 (8 removed); Exp 2: 129 (12 removed). Aha-accuracy r = 0.24 (Exp 1a) and 0.19 (Exp 2) in non-insight problems. Classic insight had higher Aha than non-insight in all three experiments (10.15 points in Exp 1). Warmth not measured.
limits: Self-report cannot separate insight as process from insight as feeling; results vary across experiments.
agent_relevance: Do not route by 'this is an insight problem'. Route by observed impasse (S6), which code can see.

source: Steyvers et al. (2024) What Large Language Models Know and What People Think They Know
finding: People over-trust default LLM explanations; matching explanation wording to the model's real confidence narrows the gap, with no gain in people's accuracy.
numbers: 301 participants over experiments. ECE: GPT-3.5 model .104, humans default .264, modified .150. AUC: model .751, humans .589, modified .694. Long explanations raise confidence (BF=25) without improving discrimination (AUC .54).
limits: Multiple-choice and short answer only; needs two LLM calls; not insight tasks.
agent_relevance: Fluent text inflates trust; a scaffold that shows a judge the agent's long reasoning would inflate confidence (G5 length normalisation).

source: Miao and Ungar (2026) Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models
finding: Asking a model to solve and rate confidence in one prompt corrupts the confidence signal. Separating the two and steering improves calibration.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, MATH. Verbalized ECE 14.9/35.1/36.0 falls to 3.7/3.3/10.7 with steering. Cosine of confidence and accuracy directions +0.26 (pure prompt) vs -0.63 (joint solve-and-rate). Probe Cohen d=1.88.
limits: 7-8B models only; verifiable QA only; steering needs weights; text says 4-7x but the table gives 3.4-10.6x.
agent_relevance: If any confidence is read it must come from a separate pass, not the solving trace. Supports keeping S6 detection in code.

source: Kumaran et al. (2026) How do LLMs Compute Verbal Confidence
finding: Mechanistic work: verbal confidence is built at answer tokens and cached, not just a readout of token probabilities. Authors read it as automatic self-evaluation.
numbers: Gemma 3 27B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Magistral Small 24B; abstract only, no numbers read.
limits: Only the abstract was read.
agent_relevance: Competing evidence: internal confidence carries signal even if verbalised confidence is poorly calibrated; a probe is a future option, not a prompt.

source: Human-like problem-solving abilities in large language models using ChatGPT (2023), Frontiers in AI
finding: ChatGPT (Jan 9 2023 version) matched the modal human score on verbal insight problems.
numbers: 30 verbal insight problems (Ansburg and Dominowski 2000): ChatGPT 7/15 practice, 5/15 transfer, 12/30 pooled; human n=20, medians 0.55 and 0.35.
limits: One model version; human n=20; verbal problems only; no confidence or warmth measure.
agent_relevance: Early evidence that raw accuracy on verbal insight items is human-range; says nothing about monitoring.

source: Assessing the nature of large language models: a caution against anthropocentrism (2023)
finding: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 did well on a few insight items but failed all analytic ones; per-item accuracy was negatively related to human accuracy.
numbers: 5 insight problems: GPT-3.5 1.5 to 3.5 correct across four runs, GPT-4 4.5/5 in one run. Item-level human 44-61%, GPT-3.5 25-75%; r = -0.63 on only four observations. Zero correct on both analytic problems.
limits: Four observations; authors say not to weight the correlation; items may be in training data.
agent_relevance: Item difficulty for models does not follow human difficulty, so human warmth norms cannot be transferred to model difficulty estimates.

source: Zhu et al. (2026) Dissecting Failure Dynamics in Large Language Model Reasoning (GUARD)
finding: Errors start at a few early transition points that coincide with token-entropy spikes; branching from the same state can still reach the right answer. GUARD probes and redirects only at spikes.
numbers: Adaptive threshold from historical entropy percentiles; eight benchmarks; ablation on R1-Distill-Qwen-7B shows momentum, inhibitory and counterfactual branches are all needed. Headline gains not captured.
limits: Abstract, method and ablation text read; no headline numbers captured.
agent_relevance: Code-detected impasse by entropy percentile, then a short local branch, fits S6 and G12.

source: Li et al. (2026) Stop When Further Reasoning Won't Help: Attention-State Adaptive Generation (ASAG)
finding: Training-free early stop from attention state instead of the model's confidence, because confidence is overconfident on hard items and underconfident on easy ones.
numbers: Nine benchmarks; on Qwen3-8B average accuracy +3.2% and nearly 40% fewer tokens.
limits: Abstract and introduction read only.
agent_relevance: Stopping from internal state beats stopping from stated confidence; supports G11 and code-side signals.

source: Bai, Cao, Ge and Yu (2025) MP: Endowing Large Language Models with Lateral Thinking, AAAI
finding: Metacognitive prompting (three-step prompt modelled on human metacognition) beats chain-of-thought on lateral-thinking sets; with GPT-4 it is reported to exceed the human score on BRAINTEASER.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo vs CoT: Sentence Puzzle +5.00, Word Puzzle +10.07, BiRdQA +6.48, RiddleSense +2.65 (percent).
limits: Search snippet only; paper not read; prompt-only gain with no verification step.
agent_relevance: A prompt-only scaffold gain on riddles; adopt only if it holds at equal tokens (G7).

source: Jiang et al. (2023) BRAINTEASER: Lateral Thinking Puzzles for Large Language Models
finding: Lateral-thinking multiple choice with consistency checks: models far below humans, and much worse when all reworded variants must be right.
numbers: Human experts about 92% on 102 questions; ChatGPT about 60-63% instance accuracy and under 40% group accuracy. Sentence 62.68, word 53.46. SemEval 2024 entries: GPT-4 with prompting 97.5% on sentence puzzles.
limits: Search snippets only; SemEval setups not comparable.
agent_relevance: Consistency across reworded variants is a code-checkable test that needs no self-report (G3).

source: Entropy and loop detectors for reasoning and agents (2025-2026): arXiv 2509.26522, 2510.08146, 2603.14251, Sotis package
finding: Several tools detect being stuck from entropy of tokens or actions (entropy after the think tag, high-entropy Wait bursts, action-loop entropy windows) and trigger early exit or a jump prompt.
numbers: No accuracy numbers read.
limits: Search snippets only; many preprints; one is a blog note and one an open-source package.
agent_relevance: Existing code-side impasse signals that could implement S6 triggers; compare at equal tokens before use.

source: Metcalfe and Wiebe (1987) Intuition in insight and noninsight problem solving
finding: Original finding: warmth rises gradually before noninsight solutions but not before insight solutions, so people cannot predict insight. Only 39 of 73 subjects gave usable data.
numbers: Per the 2016 replication paper and a search summary; not opened here.
limits: Original not opened; the 2016 magic-trick study did not replicate the warmth pattern, under weaker warmth sampling.
agent_relevance: Human anchor for the guardrail; cite as motivation, not as an LLM result.

source: Stumpers study authors (2023) LLMs versus humans on stumpers, EMNLP Findings (prompt effect)
finding: A hint prompt helped older GPT-3 models and hurt the chat models, so prompt help depends on the model.
numbers: Model x prompt interaction F(1,4)=30.82, p=0.005; main effect of prompt F(1,4)=0.023, p=0.887; chat vs GPT-3 F(1,4)=686, p=0.00001.
limits: Few models and items; 2023 models.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a metacognitive prompt transfers across models; measure per model (G7).
